\caption{\textbf{Slide encoders versus mean-pooling of their own tile embeddings on PCaBiop.} Pairs (slide encoder, tile encoder): TITAN (CONCHv1.5), MOOZY (Lunit ViT-S/8) and PRISM2 (Virchow2). Each slide encoder's published slide2vec configuration was re-run on the $1{,}324$ PCaBiop slides with its tile embeddings saved, so both arms come from one tiling: the slide arm is the slide encoder's embedding and the mean-pool arm is the unweighted mean of the same tile embeddings. Re-run slide embeddings reproduced the published ones (per-slide cosine $\geq0.999$ on every slide) for MOOZY and PRISM2, whose published embeddings form the slide arm. They did not for TITAN: $17$ of $1{,}324$ slides reproduced (minimum cosine $0.412$), so its re-run slide embeddings form the slide arm. bio bacc, median \code{CRoMa}$(m{=}5)$, $F(0)$ and $\mcode{LTM}_{10}$ are from the benchmark runner on the in-domain PANDA cohort at $k^\star$; \code{nIPD} (\%) is from the PCaBiop linear-probe sweep, in domain (PANDA) and out of domain (PAR). $\Delta$ is slide minus mean-pool: \code{CRoMa} summaries with 95\% confidence intervals from a stratified slide bootstrap (class $\times$ provider strata, $2{,}000$ replicates, one draw shared by every arm), and \code{nIPD} differences ($\pm$ the standard deviation of the $20$ paired probe replicates). Declared pairs not shown: PRISM (Virchow) and Prov-GigaPath (Prov-GigaPath).}
